Paragraph:
Translation: One who can control his senses by practicing the regulated principles of freedom can obtain the complete mercy of the Lord and thus become free from all attachment and aversion.

Purport (Excerpt): ...Although the person in full Krsna consciousness may apparently be on the sensual plane, because of his being Krsna conscious, he has no attachment to sensual activities. The Krsna conscious person is concerned only with the satisfaction of Krsna... Therefore to act or not to act is within his control...
Situation/Problem_Faced: How to live and work in a world full of sensory stimuli without either fleeing into total isolation or falling into self-indulgence.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna introduces 'regulated principles of freedom' (vidheyatma). True freedom is not absolute license or total avoidance; it is the ability to interact with the world through structured principles, transcending both compulsive attraction (raga) and bitter aversion (dvesa).
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is shown that he can remain engaged in the world—even on a battlefield—while maintaining internal purity and peace.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Structured Freedom: Living by self-imposed, constructive regulations rather than whims
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Transcending Polarities (Like/Dislike): Operating beyond emotional attachment (raga) and hatred/avoidance (dvesa)
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Healthy Engagement: Interacting with the world safely using clear boundaries

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Raga-dvesa-vimuktaih (Freedom from the dualities of attraction and repulsion)
Vidheyatma (A self-controlled soul acting under regulated principles)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: A liberated soul does not need to flee to the forest. By engaging with the world according to divine guidelines (regulations), they remain completely unpolluted. They are governed by devotion, moving beyond both selfish craving (raga) and resentful avoidance (dvesa).
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This verse redefines freedom. Real autonomy is not doing whatever you feel like in the moment; that is slavery to impulse. True freedom is the ability to navigate life using healthy, conscious boundaries (regulations) so that you are neither compulsively drawn to triggers nor paralyzed by irrational disliking.
